units.title: Finiteness of polar surface mass
units.classification: Shared sphere-calculus support interface; definitions are not theorem credit
units.statement: Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. Write \(\tau_n=\operatorname{vol}_{E_n}.\mathrm{toSphere}\), \(\sigma_n=\tau_n(S_n)^{-1}\tau_n\), and \(\mu_{n,N}=\bigotimes_i\sigma_n\); measure scaling uses the extended nonnegative-real inverse. For every natural \(n\), the actual polar measure on the unit sphere has finite total mass. This is a proved instance inherited from the polar-measure API.
assumptions: Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
The stated property concerns the actual defined measure; its normalization inputs are established by the proof, not supplied as assumptions.

steps.title: Use finiteness of the polar construction
steps.text: The polar-measure API supplies a finite measure for Euclidean volume in this finite-dimensional ambient space. The instance applies that result to the displayed measure.
